subject: Slate renewal: traffic shift, rightsize options, and ratecard bridge
messages:
From: Alex Reid <alex@slate.ai>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@slate.ai>
Date: 2027-11-13T14:02:00-08:00
Subject: Renewal planning & mid-quarter traffic shift

Hi Tessa,

Quick note from our side — we just finished a spike test for a new multimodal feature and saw a sustained 2.8x increase in token consumption on November 9–11. The platform handled latency OK but our monthly run rate is now trending well above our committed tier for Q1.

We'd like to lock the renewal window but also talk tradeoffs: can we adjust model mix for inference (move bulk batch calls to a smaller variant), get a short-term bridge for overage protection, and potentially move to a quarterly commit for Q1 while we stabilize?

Priya (cc) will share the usage report. Can you propose 2–3 options (term/commit/burst credits) and any immediate suggestions to reduce unit cost? We have a procurement review on Nov 18 — ideal to have a clear path before then.

Thanks,
Alex

--
Alex Reid
CEO, Slate.ai
alex@slate.ai

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
To: Alex Reid <alex@slate.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@slate.ai>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-11-13T17:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning & mid-quarter traffic shift

Alex — thanks for the heads-up and the report (received).

Preliminary read: the spike is concentrated in inference-heavy endpoints (batch transform + high-beam reranking). We'll propose three paths:

1) Short bridge + burst credits (30 days) to cover Nov–Dec overage while we rightsize model mix.
2) Term swap: move to a quarterly committed tier for Q1 (lower list price per-token at higher committed volume) with an opt-out after Q1 if consumption normalizes.
3) Model-mix optimization + KV prefix caching to reduce repeated token generation for common prompts — ops-led change with immediate token savings.

I'll loop Marissa and Ben to price the bridge and term-swap options and include a quick ROI sketch. Can we schedule a 30-min working session tomorrow (11/14) or Monday?

Attaching: slate_q3_usage_summary.csv (Priya), and a short latency-sample PDF our infra team captured.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
T: +1 415-555-0197

Attachments: slate_q3_usage_summary.csv (summary), latency-sample.pdf (sample traces)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-11-13T20:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning & mid-quarter traffic shift

Adding ops/finance context from our side — high-level numbers: if Slate's Nov run-rate holds, they will overspend ~38% vs current commit. Two quick countermeasures I recommend we price:

- 30-day bridge: fixed burst credit bucket (~$18k) + 20% discount on overage tokens during the bridge window.
- Quarterly commit: tier Q1-3 (3 months) at ~15% list discount in exchange for a 1.5x commit multiplier vs current monthly run-rate.

Ben, can you draft the ratecard math and a simple ROI table (savings vs incremental commit) we can include in the meeting deck? Karthik, please confirm SLA implications if they switch to a higher committed tier (latency / reserved capacity).

-Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-11-14T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning & mid-quarter traffic shift

Attaching draft ROI table below (pasted) and the ratecard scenarios.

Scenario A — 30-day bridge
- Burst credit: $18,000 (one-time)
- Effective overage rate during bridge: $0.00008 / token (20% off list)
- Estimated tokens consumed in bridge window: 1.2B
- Incremental cost vs no action: +$14,400 (but capped with credit)

Scenario B — Q1 quarterly commit
- Commit: 3.0B tokens / quarter (1.5x current monthly run-rate aggregated)
- Effective committed price: $0.000065 / token (15% discount)
- Estimated delta vs status quo: +$9,000 monthly but ~25% per-token savings on the incremental volume

Quick take: If Slate expects high variance but wants short-term protection, the bridge preserves cash flow and gives time for model-mix changes. If they expect elevated normalized consumption, the quarterly commit is cleaner and reduces unit cost.

I'll build a slide with the numbers.

--
Ben Carter
Account Economics, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, Alex Reid <alex@slate.ai>
Date: 2027-11-15T09:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning & mid-quarter traffic shift

Alex — quick note on SLA/reserved capacity: moving to a higher committed tier for Q1 will allow us to reserve additional pool capacity in the region (us-west-2). Practically: 95th percentile latency targets improve by ~40–60 ms for high-concurrency workloads under the reserved pool. That matters for your reranking endpoints.

Operationally, we can enable a two-week preferrable routing change (route batch jobs to preemptible pools with smaller models) while preserving low-latency paths for real-time endpoints. This supports the model-mix shift Tessa mentioned.

I'll be on the call to run through the impact map.

-Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Head of Product Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Priya Shah <priya@slate.ai>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, Alex Reid <alex@slate.ai>
Date: 2027-11-16T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning & mid-quarter traffic shift

Thanks all — the team reviewed Ben's numbers and Karthik's notes. We're inclined to take the 30-day bridge immediately to avoid procurement friction and run a parallel model-mix pilot (batch -> smaller variant) during the bridge. If the pilot shows >20% token reduction after two weeks, we'll convert to the quarterly commit for Q1.

I've attached the PO for the bridge window (PO_2028-Q1.pdf) and scheduled the procurement review for Nov 18 at 11:00 AM PT. Can Redwood confirm the bridge activation timeline and email a one-page summary of the bridge terms we can share with procurement?

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Priya

--
Priya Shah
VP Product, Slate.ai

Attachments: PO_2028-Q1.pdf
